name: Clearing Transactional Data on Odoo 17
body:
Removing Transactional Data from Odoo 17

While Preserving Studio Customizations

Scope of this guide: Sales, Accounting, Inventory, Purchase, MRP, HR/Payroll/Attendance/Time Off (transactional records only — employees and contracts are preserved by design), and Helpdesk. Does not cover Project — extend the model list in Section 12 if that's in scope for you.

Hard requirement: Run this on a staging/duplicate branch only. Never against production. This guide assumes Odoo.sh with shell access via odoo-bin shell.

Contents

Removing Transactional Data from Odoo 17While Preserving Studio CustomizationsContents0. Why you can't just delete rows in SQL1. Studio customizations are never at risk from this process2. Pre-flight checks3. Deletion order — Sales / Accounting / Inventory (children before parents)Step 1 — PaymentsStep 2 — InvoicesStep 3 — PickingsStep 4 — Sale orders4. Commit after every stage — do not wait until the end5. Final verification6. Check for orphaned references in Studio-customized models7. Purchase8. MRP (if installed)9. Inventory — beyond pickings10. HR / Payroll / Attendance / Time OffPayslipsTime OffAttendanceVerify employees/contracts are untouched, transactional data is gone11. Helpdesk12. Notes for extending further (e.g. Project)


0. Why you can't just delete rows in SQL

Posted accounting entries in Odoo 17 carry integrity protections:

  • Hash chain (restrict_mode_hash_table on account.journal) — anti-fraud sequencing that breaks if entries are altered/deleted outside the ORM.
  • Fiscal/tax lock dates (env.company.fiscalyear_lock_date, tax_lock_date) — block resetting posted entries to draft.
  • Foreign keys everywhere — sale orders link to invoices, deliveries, stock moves, valuation layers, payments, and (if you have Studio fields) potentially custom models you don't know about yet.

Direct SQL DELETE bypasses all of this and leaves orphaned rows with no error to warn you. Always go through the ORM (odoo-bin shell), which enforces cascades and constraints correctly.

1. Studio customizations are never at risk from this process

Deleting sale.order, account.move, stock.picking records does not touch ir.model.fields (state='manual'), custom views, automation rules, or approval rules — those are schema/metadata, not transactional data. What can happen is a Studio-added field on some other model (e.g. a custom "Sales Order" lookup field on helpdesk.ticket) ends up holding a dangling ID after you delete the record it pointed to. That's a data-orphan issue in a different model, not damage to the customization itself. Section 6 covers how to check for this.

2. Pre-flight checks

Run these before touching anything, in one line each — never stack multiple expressions in one cell and only read the last Out[], you will lose data from the ones before it.

env.company.fiscalyear_lock_date
env.company.tax_lock_date
env['account.journal'].search([]).mapped(lambda j: (j.name, j.restrict_mode_hash_table))

If any journal you're clearing shows restrict_mode_hash_table = True, or either lock date is set and covers your invoice dates, resolve that first (temporarily clear the lock date on a staging branch — env.company.write({'fiscalyear_lock_date': False})).

3. Deletion order — Sales / Accounting / Inventory (children before parents)

  1. account.payment
  2. account.move (invoices/bills/entries)
  3. stock.picking (cascades stock.move, stock.move.line)
  4. sale.order

Do not skip ahead — deleting a parent before its children throws constraint errors or, worse, silently fails in a way you won't notice until later.

Step 1 — Payments

payments = env['account.payment'].search([])
payments.mapped('state')

Unreconcile before cancelling if any are paid/in_process:

moves_to_unreconcile = payments.mapped('move_id.line_ids').filtered(lambda l: l.reconciled)
moves_to_unreconcile.remove_move_reconcile()
payments.action_cancel()
payments.unlink()
env.cr.commit()

Step 2 — Invoices

invoices = env['account.move'].search([('move_type', 'in', ['out_invoice', 'in_invoice', 'out_refund', 'in_refund', 'entry'])])
invoices.mapped('state')

button_draft() requires the whole batch to be in posted or cancel state — filter first, or it throws "Only posted/cancelled journal entries can be reset to draft."

posted_invoices = invoices.filtered(lambda m: m.state == 'posted')
posted_invoices.button_draft()
env.cr.commit()

Re-query — don't trust that the command "ran without error" means it succeeded:

env['account.move'].search([('move_type', 'in', ['out_invoice', 'in_invoice', 'out_refund', 'in_refund', 'entry'])]).mapped('state')

Once everything shows draft or cancel:

env['account.move'].search([('move_type', 'in', ['out_invoice', 'in_invoice', 'out_refund', 'in_refund', 'entry'])]).unlink()
env.cr.commit()

Step 3 — Pickings

pickings = env['stock.picking'].search([])
pickings.mapped('state')

If none show done, this is safe — no valuation layers to reverse:

pickings.action_cancel()
env.cr.commit()
pickings.unlink()
env.cr.commit()

Note — If any show done, stop and check stock.valuation.layer for entries tied to them before proceeding — that's a bigger unwind this guide doesn't cover.

Step 4 — Sale orders

Orders may be locked — clear that first:

orders = env['sale.order'].search([])
orders.write({'locked': False})
env.cr.commit()

Known bug — calling action_cancel() on a multi-record recordset can throw ValueError: Expected singleton because Odoo's cancel-wizard check (_show_cancel_wizard() → ensure_one()) isn't written for batch calls in some paths. Loop instead:

for order in orders:
    order.action_cancel()
env.cr.commit()
orders.mapped('state')

Known bug #2 — action_cancel() can silently no-op — it returns a wizard action dict (meant for the UI to render a confirmation dialog) instead of actually cancelling, and in a headless shell that dict does nothing. Always re-check state after calling it; don't assume success just because no exception was raised. If state is still 'sale' after the loop, and you've already confirmed there are no real linked documents left to legitimately need review, bypass the wizard directly:

orders.write({'state': 'cancel'})
env.cr.commit()

Then delete:

orders.unlink()
env.cr.commit()

4. Commit after every stage — do not wait until the end

The shell does not reliably keep a long-lived transaction alive across a whole session. In practice: some statements auto-commit individually, others don't, and a dropped connection (idle timeout, network blip) mid-session can silently discard everything since the last real commit — with no warning, and with partial/inconsistent results (some records reset, others not) rather than a clean all-or-nothing rollback.

Rule: call env.cr.commit() after every stage (payments, invoices, pickings, orders), and re-query state before starting the next stage. Never assume that because a command ran earlier in the session, its effect is still there.

5. Final verification

Run each line separately — do not chain them in one cell and trust the last Out[] to represent all of them:

print(env['sale.order'].search_count([]))
print(env['account.move'].search_count([('move_type', 'in', ['out_invoice', 'in_invoice', 'out_refund', 'in_refund', 'entry'])]))
print(env['stock.picking'].search_count([]))
print(env['account.payment'].search_count([]))

All four should read 0.

6. Check for orphaned references in Studio-customized models

Deleting the records above doesn't touch Studio field definitions, but a stored Studio many2one field on some other model may now hold a dead ID. Find every Studio field that points at what you deleted:

studio_fields = env['ir.model.fields'].search([('state', '=', 'manual')])
targets = studio_fields.filtered(lambda f: f.relation in ['sale.order', 'account.move', 'stock.picking', 'account.move.line'])
for f in targets:
    print(f.model, f.name, f.relation, f.ttype, f.store)

Ignore:

  • Fields living on the models you just deleted (e.g. a field on account.move itself) — moot, the parent record is gone.
  • Fields with store: False — these recompute live and can't hold a stale ID.

Check the rest — stored many2one/one2many fields on surviving models — for dangling references:

env['<model_name>'].search([]).mapped(lambda r: (r.id, getattr(r, '<field_name>').id if getattr(r, '<field_name>') else False))

If any show an ID that no longer exists, clear that field on the affected record (record.write({'<field_name>': False})) — this fixes the orphaned data, it does not touch the Studio customization itself.

7. Purchase

Mirrors Sales — expect the same wizard/singleton bugs from Section 3, Step 4 to apply here too.

bills = env['account.move'].search([('move_type', '=', 'in_invoice')])
bills.mapped('state')
posted_bills = bills.filtered(lambda m: m.state == 'posted')
posted_bills.button_draft()
env.cr.commit()
env['account.move'].search([('move_type', '=', 'in_invoice')]).unlink()
env.cr.commit()
incoming = env['stock.picking'].search([('picking_type_id.code', '=', 'incoming')])
incoming.action_cancel()
env.cr.commit()
incoming.unlink()
env.cr.commit()
pos = env['purchase.order'].search([])
pos.mapped('state')
for po in pos:
    po.button_cancel()
env.cr.commit()
pos.mapped('state')   # confirm cancelled before unlinking — don't assume the loop worked
pos.unlink()
env.cr.commit()

Cross-module orphan check specific to Purchase — you already found two Studio fields linking Purchase back to Sales: purchase.order.x_studio_subcontracting_so and x_purchase.request.line.make.purchase.order.x_subcontracting_so, both pointing at sale.order. Since sale.order records are already gone, check these now for dangling IDs, same pattern as Section 6:

env['purchase.order'].search([]).mapped(lambda r: (r.id, r.x_studio_subcontracting_so.id if r.x_studio_subcontracting_so else False))

8. MRP (if installed)

Children before parents: workorders, then productions, then the resulting stock moves.

env['mrp.workorder'].search([]).unlink()
env.cr.commit()
productions = env['mrp.production'].search([])
productions.mapped('state')

If any show done, they've already posted consumed/produced stock moves to valuation — treat like a done picking (Section 3, Step 3) and check stock.valuation.layer before proceeding, rather than cancelling blind.

productions.action_cancel()
env.cr.commit()
productions.unlink()
env.cr.commit()

9. Inventory — beyond pickings

Deleting stock.picking/stock.move (Section 3) does not clear on-hand quantities — those live in separate, persistent records:

print(env['stock.quant'].search_count([]))
print(env['stock.valuation.layer'].search_count([]))
print(env['stock.lot'].search_count([]))

If you want inventory counts genuinely zeroed (not just move history cleared), that needs an explicit inventory adjustment to zero, or direct cleanup if this is meant to be a blank slate — decide this deliberately, since zeroing quants on a database that still has other live data could misrepresent stock on hand. Orphaned stock.lot records (no remaining moves referencing them) can generally be unlinked once you've confirmed no stock.quant still references them.

10. HR / Payroll / Attendance / Time Off

Scope: transactional records only. Employees (hr.employee) and contracts (hr.contract) are preserved — do not delete or modify them.

Payroll can generate its own account.move entries (move_type='entry'), which may overlap with what you already cleared in the Accounting sweep (Section 3, Step 2). Check before assuming either way:

env['account.move'].search_count([('move_type', '=', 'entry')])

If non-zero, check payslip.move_id on the payslips below before unlinking, so you don't leave a dangling account.move with no payslip pointing back at it (or vice versa).

Payslips

Resist deletion once done/paid, cancel first:

payslips = env['hr.payslip'].search([])
payslips.mapped('state')
payslips.action_payslip_cancel()
env.cr.commit()
payslips.unlink()
env.cr.commit()

Batch runs can block deletion of their child payslips if left in close state:

env['hr.payslip.run'].search([]).mapped('state')
env['hr.payslip.run'].search([]).unlink()
env.cr.commit()

Time Off

Has an approval workflow; confirm/validate states resist deletion the same way locked sale orders did:

leaves = env['hr.leave'].search([])
leaves.mapped('state')
leaves.action_refuse()   # or action_draft() — check which action is available in your version
env.cr.commit()
leaves.unlink()
env.cr.commit()

Clear allocations too if leave balances should reset, not just requests:

env['hr.leave.allocation'].search([]).unlink()
env.cr.commit()

Attendance

No approval workflow, straight delete:

env['hr.attendance'].search([]).unlink()
env.cr.commit()

Verify employees/contracts are untouched, transactional data is gone

print(env['hr.employee'].search_count([]))    # should match your count from before this section
print(env['hr.contract'].search_count([]))    # should match your count from before this section
print(env['hr.payslip'].search_count([]))     # should be 0
print(env['hr.leave'].search_count([]))       # should be 0
print(env['hr.attendance'].search_count([]))  # should be 0

Then run the Studio orphan check (Section 6) filtered to hr.payslip, hr.leave, hr.attendance as the relation — a Studio field linking hr.employee to a payslip/leave record for reporting may now point at nothing. That's expected (the employee side is intact; only the far end is gone) but worth confirming rather than assuming.

11. Helpdesk

No known wizard bugs on this model — you already confirmed (Section 6, first pass) that no ticket references the deleted sale orders, so this is low-risk:

tickets = env['helpdesk.ticket'].search([])
tickets.unlink()
env.cr.commit()

12. Notes for extending further (e.g. Project)

The same pattern applies: find children before parents, check restrict_mode_hash_table and lock dates for any new journals involved, commit after every stage, and re-run the Studio field orphan check (Section 6) with the additional models added to the relation in [...] filter. Expect the same two action_cancel()-style bugs (singleton error on batch calls, silent wizard no-op) on any model that inherits a similar cancel/wizard pattern.

Internal runbook — staging branches only. Verify against your specific Odoo 17 point release before running unattended.

Basic Steps

Analytical Tags

 Analytics tags are user-defined labels or markers that can be applied to various records within Odoo. These tags are flexible and can be customized to reflect different aspects of your business operations, such as product attributes, customer segments, project stages, etc.

Analytical tags template

AX_Analytical_Tag.xlsx
xlsx


Inventory Module


Importing data into the Inventory module of Odoo 15 can streamline the process of populating your inventory with initial stock levels, product details, and other relevant information. Here’s a step-by-step guide on major tables data imports effectively.

Products Table

Efficiently populate your product catalog with details such as product names, descriptions, prices, categories, and more.

Products table template with Cost Price

Product Template_to Cost Update_N110.xlsx
xlsx


Warehouse Table

Inventory -> Configuration -> warehouse

Importing warehouses into Odoo 15 allows you to set up and manage your physical locations where inventory is stored.

Warehouse table template

Warehouse (stock.warehouse) (3).xlsx
xlsx


Work Center Table

Odoo 15 allows you to define the various stations or work areas where manufacturing operations take place. Different employees can be assign to different work stations and freely change them accroding to the production floor operations.



BOM Table with Operations

Bill of Materials (BOM) into Odoo 15 allows you to define the structure of your products, specifying the components and quantities required for production. However,  Bill of Materials (BOM) with operations into Odoo 15 allows you to define not only the components and quantities required for production but also the specific operations or work centers involved in manufacturing the product.


BOM Table Template

Inventory stock count Table

mport initial stock quantities effectively into Odoo, ensuring that your inventory records are accurate and reflect the correct starting balances for your products across all warehouses configured in your instance.


Inventory stock count template

JAM_Quants (stock quant) With Serial_Template.xlsx
xlsx


Payroll Module


Payroll -> Configuration -> Structures / Structure Types

A salary structure in Odoo refers to the framework or configuration that defines how an employee's total compensation (salary) is calculated and distributed. It typically includes various components such as basic salary, allowances, deductions, bonuses, and other benefits.


A salary type in Odoo refers to the categorization or classification of different types of salary components within a salary structure. It helps in organizing and managing how different types of payments and deductions contribute to an employee's total salary.



Salary Rule

A salary rule refers to a specific rule or calculation method applied to determine how an employee's salary or earnings are computed. These rules are configured within the payroll system to automate the calculation of wages based on various factors such as hours worked, rates, allowances, deductions, and other components.

name: Odoo + Claude Code + Playwright Development Environment
body:
Odoo + Claude Code + Playwright Development Environment1. Environment Overview1.1 Architecture2. Prerequisites2.1 Docker Desktop - Optional2.2 VS Code2.3 Node.js (v18 or later)2.4 Git2.5 Git Bash (included with Git for Windows)2.6 Claude CodeReverse The Process!3. Claude code Setup3.1 Running Claude Code Locally4. Setup Claude Code Spec Workflow - Odoo5. Setup Playwright-CLIOptional (If you need a Local Instance of Odoo)6. Getting the Project7. Start the Docker Environment7.1 Useful Docker Commands:8. Accessing Odoo8.1 Open Odoo in your browser8.2 Log in8.3 Setup the Database (First Time Only)

Odoo + Claude Code + Playwright Development Environment

1. Environment Overview

This development environment combines three major tools:

Odoo 17: ERP Platform - the application being developed and tested

Claude Code: AI-powered development assistant for business Odoo modules

Playwright: End-to-end browser test automation for Odoo UI Testing

1.1 Architecture

Your Windows Machine (Host)

  D:\odoo-dev-claude\                                   

├── .env                 ← Odoo Login Details

├── docker-compose.yml

├── Dockerfile

├── odoo-project\        ← Mounted into Docker

└── tests\               ← Playwright E2E tests (host)

2. Prerequisites

Install the following on your Windows machine before proceeding

2.1 Docker Desktop - Optional

Required to run all three containers.

1. Download from: https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/ 

2. Run the installer and follow the prompts.

3. During setup, enable "Use WSL 2 instead of Hyper-V" (recommended).

4. After installation, start Docker Desktop and wait for the whale icon in the taskbar to show "Docker Desktop is running".

Verify installation:

docker --version
docker compose version

2.2 VS Code

1. Download from: https://code.visualstudio.com/download

2. Run the installer and follow the prompts.

2.3 Node.js (v18 or later)

Required for running Playwright E2E tests on the host machine.

1. Download the LTS installer from: https://nodejs.org/ 

2. Run the installer with default options.

Verify installation:

node --version
npm --version

2.4 Git

Required for version control.

Using winget (Windows Package Manager):

winget install Git.Git

Or download from: https://git-scm.com/downloads/win 

Verify installation:

git --version

2.5 Git Bash (included with Git for Windows)

The `setup.sh` script requires a bash-compatible shell. Git Bash is installed automatically with Git for Windows. You can find it in your Start Menu as "Git Bash".

2.6 Claude Code

Run the below command in a terminal

npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

Error: If you run into the below error while trying to install.

about_Execution_Policies at https:/go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=135170.
At line:1 char:1
+ npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
+ ~~~
    + CategoryInfo          : SecurityError: (:) [], PSSecurityException
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : UnauthorizedAccess

Open powershell as administrator and run the below command and try installing claude code again

Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned

Reverse The Process!

3. Claude code Setup

Claude Code is the AI development assistant that helps you build Odoo modules using the spec workflow.

3.1 Running Claude Code Locally

Claude code is installed globally on the host machine.

Navigate to the project directory from a terminal

cd D:/claude-code-spec-workflow-odoo-jinasena

Start Claude Code

claude

4. Setup Claude Code Spec Workflow - Odoo

1. Run the below command to install the Odoo edition globally

npm i -g @stanleykao72/claude-code-spec-workflow-odoo

2. Run the setup command in your project directory

# Install the Claude Code workflow with Odoo integration
claude-code-spec-workflow-odoo setup
# or using npx
npx @stanleykao72/claude-code-spec-workflow-odoo setup

3. For Odoo projects, also run the specialized Odoo environment setup

claude-code-spec-workflow-odoo odoo-setup
# or using npx
npx @stanleykao72/claude-code-spec-workflow-odoo odoo

5. Setup Playwright-CLI

1. Run the below command to install Playwright.

npm init -y
npm install --save-dev @playwright/test
npx playwright install

2. Basic Usage ​

Run all tests:

npx playwright test

Run a specific file:

npx playwright test tests/example.spec.ts

Run in headed mode (see the browser):

npx playwright test --headed

To open last HTML report

npx playwright show-report

3. Key CLI Flags

FlagPurpose
--headedRun with visible browser
--debugOpen Playwright Inspector
--uiOpen interactive UI mode
--grep "name"Filter tests by name
--workers NSet parallel workers
--retries NRetry failed tests
--reporter=htmlGenerate HTML report

body:
Issue with User-Defined Defaults for all Studio Customizations in Multi-company Environments

Issue with User-Defined Defaults for all Studio Customizations in Multi-company EnvironmentsIntroductionBackgroundIssue DescriptionImpactSolution ImplementationTechnical AdjustmentsConclusion Recommendations


Introduction

This document provides a detailed explanation of the customizations performed in the Odoo ERP system, specifically within the HelpDesk, Sales, and Purchase modules. It also addresses the issues encountered during the implementation of these customizations in a multi-company environment and outlines the solutions applied to resolve these issues.


Background

In the initial development phase, customizations were made using Odoo Studio to streamline various processes across the HelpDesk, Sales, and Purchase modules. These customizations involved setting default values for specific fields, which were used in custom logic to automate and optimize certain workflows. The default values were applied directly through Odoo Studio’s "Set Default" feature, which simplified the implementation process. However, these default values were user-defined, meaning they were specific to the user who set them and not universally applicable across all users or companies.


Issue Description

The system worked seamlessly in a single-company environment. However, when the organization expanded its operations to include a second company, a critical issue emerged: the default values set during the initial development were not recognized in the newly created company. This led to a breakdown in the custom logic that relied on these default values, causing disruptions in automated processes and inconsistencies in data handling across the different modules.

Impact

  • HelpDesk Module: Automated ticket assignment and categorization processes failed to execute correctly, leading to manual intervention.
  • Sales/Purchase Modules: Application areas that depended on default values were not applied, resulting in incorrect pricing and order processing. Order validation processes were disrupted, affecting procurement workflows.​

Solution Implementation

To resolve the issue, a three-pronged approach was adopted.:


  • Set the Company ID to null if the User-Defined Defaults are common across all companies:


​If the User-Defined Defaults for multiple companies have a one-to-one match, the following simple approach can be followed.


Go to the User-Defined Defaults list page and filter the records by the company where they were originally created as below.

​ ​ ​


​ Make the Company field blank either manually or by using a bulk template upload, depending on the number of records available.

​


  • Setting User-Defined Defaults for the New Company:

​The default values were recreated through the "User-defined Default" option available in the Settings > Technical > Actions menu, allowing ​for consistent application across the new company's operations.

​

​ ​The user can simply click the 'Create' button if they need to create a User-defined Default individually.

​


​In cases where a new company is created, it is easier and recommended to create all the User-defined Defaults in bulk for the new company. ​Otherwise, there is a chance of missing some if they are created individually as explained in the previous step. Therefore, in such scenarios, go ​to the User-defined Defaults list page and follow the instructions below.


​Filter the User-defined Defaults list page by the required existing company as shown below.  

​

​Once the list page is filtered, select all the filtered fields and export them to an Excel file as shown below.

​


​Once the file is downloaded, change the company to the newly created one and save the template for import, as shown below.

​


​Once the file is ready, go to the User-defined Defaults list page and import the data as shown below.

​

​Click the 'Upload File' button to upload the template.

​


​Ensure the correct field mapping is set before uploading and click on Import button, as shown below.

​


​Once the template is successfully uploaded, the user-defined default values will be applicable for the newly created company.

​

​

​ Another way to recreate default values for the new company is to use the 'Set Default' option available at the form level when debugging    ​mode is activated. This ensures that the necessary default values are present in the context of the new company.

​

​

​​

  • Adjusting Custom Logic:

​The custom logic in the affected modules was reviewed and modified to accommodate the multi-company setup. This involved ensuring that  ​the logic could correctly identify and apply the appropriate default values based on the active company context.

​Tests were conducted to verify that the customizations now functioned correctly in both the original and the newly created companies, with ​default values being applied consistently regardless of the active company.


Technical Adjustments

  • HelpDesk/ Sales/ Purchase Modules: Adjusted the automation scripts. calculated fields accordingly to reference the new default values specific to each company.


Conclusion

The issue was successfully resolved by creating user-defined defaults specific to the newly created company and adjusting the existing logic to ensure compatibility in a multi-company environment. These changes have stabilized the processes across all modules, ensuring consistent and reliable operations within both companies.


Recommendations

Future Developments: When setting default values in Odoo, especially in a multi-company environment, it is crucial to use company-specific settings and thoroughly test the logic across all companies.

What is MPS?

The Master Production Schedule (MPS) is a priority plan for manufacturing and the main source of the Materials Requirements Plan (MRP). Along with the bill of materials, the MPS can determine what components need to be purchased based on manufacturing quantity. The MPS indicates what, when, and how many items to produce.

when all information is entered, Click SAVE

About Rows

Starting Inventory  ​ ​ :​Quantity on hand while starting

Demand Forecast ​ :​​ Estimated demand

Actual Demand ​ ​ :​ Confirmed demand

Indirect Demand Forecast ​ :​ Estimated demand of indirect product / components

To Replenish ​ ​ ​ :​ Quantity to replenish based on MO / PO

Actual Replenishment ​ :​ Quantity being replenished based on MO / PO

Forecasted Stock ​ ​ :​ Estimated quantity in stock till the end of period

Available to Promise ​ :​ Quantity promised to be available for sale



The route must be set for the product that you are adding to Master Production Schedule. The route should be 'Manufacturing' then only it can generate the MO on replenishment.


Exsample.

  • Selected Product is N110T/1N
  • On hand Quantity is 02.

  • Planning Details


  • System Generated Details

  • Forecasted Demand


​Forecasted Demand is the estimated demand of stock for the current month. This value has to be entered manually.

  • uggested Replenishment

​Suggested Replenishment is the amount to be replenished through a purchase order or manufacturing order.  

  • Forecasted Stock

​  Forecasted Stock is the measure of product quantity that we target to have in the stock till the end of the month. This forecasted stock will be the opening stock for the next period or month.   


    • Here the source of MO can be seen as MPS(Master Production Schedule ), since MO created from the Master Production Schedule.

Applied  rule can also be changed from the Master Production Schedule by clicking on the gray circular point displayed nearer to the forecast stock.


How the calculation is working according to the below Example.


​The  opening stock for the first month (April) is 2. The minimum replenishment is set to 48. Since the forecasted stock for April is 50. The starting inventory for the next period or month May is the forecasted stock of the previous month,it is 50. And the forecasted stock is 50, so we have to produce 48 units for April.

​​Now let us add the forecasted demand. We know forecasted demand is the estimated quantity for the current month. we have demand for 10 products already. So at forecasted demand we manually entered 10 for the first month.

After forecasted demand enters the value for replenishment already changes. we have to replenish 58 products to make the forecasted stock as 50 since 10 is in demand and may be sold out. As per equation the calculation is,

Forecasted stock = Starting Inventory - Forecasted Demand  + Suggested Replenishment.

Forecasted stock ​= 2-10 + 58 

​ ​ ​= -8 + 58 

​ ​ ​= 50


 

  • Master Production Schedule cells shows in different colors

​Gray: The order for replenishing has already been produced, and its quantity still matches actual quantity, that is ​ ​actual replenishment and suggested replenishment are the same.

​Green: Quantity of goods to be replenished in order to meet the expected safety stock, taking into account the ​ ​forecasted demand and the indirect demand forecast.

​RED: ​The order for replenishment has already been produced, and its quantity of current data was too high.

​Orange: The order for replenishment has already been produced, and its quantity of current data was too low.

Lead Times


there are several types of lead times. Each is calculated based on various indicators. Before going through the configuration, here is a brief summary of how lead times are calculated and what they are:

  • Customer Lead Time: the customer lead time is the default duration you set. Therefore, the expected date on the sales orders is today + customer lead time.
  • Sales Security Lead Time: the purpose is to be ready shipping that many days before the actual commitment taken with the customer. Then, the default scheduled date on the delivery order is SO delivery date - Security Lead Time.
  • Purchase Security Lead Time: margin of error for vendor lead times. When the system generates Purchase Orders for procuring products, they will be scheduled that many days earlier to cope with unexpected vendor delays.
  • Purchase Delivery Lead Time: this is the expected time between a PO being confirmed and the receipt of the ordered products. The Receipt scheduled date - Vendor delivery date is the default PO Order By date.
  • Days to Purchase: number of days the purchasing department takes to validate a PO. If another RFQ to the same vendor is already opened, Odoo adds the line to the RFQ instead of creating a new one. Then, the specific date is set on the line.
  • Manufacturing Lead Time: this is the expected time it takes to manufacture a product. This lead time is independent of the quantity to produce and does not take the routing time into account.
  • Manufacturing Security Lead Time: additional time to mitigate the risk of a manufacturing delay. In case of a Replenish to Order, the Delivery Order scheduled date - Manufacturing Lead Time - Manufacturing Security Lead Time is the default Manufacturing Order planned date.

Sales - Lead Times

In the Sales app, there is an option called Delivery Date. It allows seeing an additional field on the sales orders, Expected Date. This one is automatically computed based on the different lead times previously configured.

If the set up Delivery Date is earlier than the the Expected Date, a warning message is displayed.

But, for all of this properly working, it is still necessary to configure all the lead times that could occur.

Customer Lead Time

The Customer Lead Time is the time needed for your product to go from your warehouse to the customer place. It can be configured on any product by going to Sales ‣ Products ‣ Products. There, open your product form, go in the inventory tab, and add your Customer Lead Time.

For example, product B is ordered on the 2nd of April but the Customer Lead Time is two days. In that case, the expected delivery date is the 4th of April.

Security Lead Time

In sales, Security Lead Time corresponds to backup days to ensure you are able to deliver the products in time. The purpose is to be ready shipping earlier in order to arrive on time.

The number of security days is subtracted from the calculation to compute a scheduled date earlier than the one promised to the customer.

To set this up, go to Inventory ‣ Configuration ‣ Settings and enable the feature Security Lead Time for Sales.

For example, product B is scheduled to be delivered on the 6th of April but the Security Lead Time is one day. In that case, the scheduled date for the delivery order is the 5th of April.

Deliver several products

In many cases, customers order several products at the same time. Those can have different lead times but still need to be delivered, at once or separately. Fortunately, Odoo can help you handle these cases easily.

From the Other Info tab of your Sale Order, you can choose between When all products are ready and As soon as possible. The first one is to deliver products at once, while the second is to deliver them separately.

For example, products A and B are ordered at the same time. A has 8 lead days and B has 5. With the first option, the Expected Date is calculated based on the product with the most lead days, here A. If the order is confirmed on the 2nd of April, then the Expected Date is on the 10th of April.

With the second option, the Expected Date is calculated based on the product with the least customer lead days. In this example, B is the product with the least lead days. So, the Expected Date is on the 7th of April.

Purchase - Lead Times

Supplier Lead Time

The Supplier Lead Time is the time needed for a product you purchased to be delivered. To configure it, open a product from Purchase ‣ Products ‣ Products and add a vendor under the Purchase tab.

By clicking on Add a line, a new window is displayed. You can specify the Delivery Lead Time there. If done so, the delivery day for every purchase of that product is now equal to Date of the Purchase Order + Delivery Lead Time.

 Note

It is possible to add different vendors and, thus, different lead times depending on the vendor.

Security Lead Time

The Security Lead Time for purchase follows the same logic as the one for Sales, except that you are the customer. Then, it is the margin of error for your supplier to deliver your order.

To set up Security Lead Time for purchase, go to Inventory ‣ Configuration ‣ Settings and enable the feature.

Doing so, every time the system generates purchase orders, those are scheduled that many days earlier to cope with unexpected vendor delays.

Manufacturing - Lead Times

Manufacturing Lead Time

The Manufacturing Lead Time is the time needed to manufacture the product. To specify it, open the Inventory tab of your product form and add the number of days the manufacturing takes.

When working with Manufacturing Lead Times, the Deadline Start of the MO is Commitment Date - Manufacturing Lead Time. For example, the MO’s deadline start date for an order having a commitment date on the 10th of July is June 27th.

Security Lead Time

The Security Lead Time for manufacturing allows generating manufacturing orders earlier to cope with the risk of manufacturing delays.

To enable it, go to Manufacturing ‣ Configuration ‣ Settings and tick Security Lead Time.

For example, a customer orders B with a delivery date scheduled on the 20th of June. The Manufacturing Lead Time is 14 days and the Security Lead Time is 3 days, so the manufacturing of B needs to start at the latest on the 3rd of June, which is the MO’s planned date.

Global Example

Here is a configuration:

  • 1 day of security lead time for Sales
  • 2 days of security lead time for Manufacturing
  • 3 days of manufacturing lead time
  • 1 day of security lead time for Purchase
  • 4 days of supplier lead time

Let’s say that a customer orders B on the 1st of September and the delivery date is planned to be within 20 days (September 20th). In such a scenario, here is when all the various steps are triggered.

  • September 1st: the sales order is created
  • September 10th: the deadline to order components from the supplier because of the manufacturing process (4 days of supplier lead time)
  • September 13th: the reception of the product from the supplier (1 day of security lead time for Purchase)
  • September 14th: the deadline start date for the manufacturing (19th - 3 days of manufacturing lead time - 2 days of security lead time for Manufacturing)
  • September 19th: the expected date on the delivery order form (1 day of security lead time for sales)

What is Inventory ROUTE and RULES.

In Odoo, the inventory route is a method used to define the path that a product takes from its source, such as a supplier or manufacturing location, to its destination, such as a warehouse or customer.  The inventory route is a key element in the inventory management process as it helps in determining the stock movements, lead times, and overall inventory flow. In Odoo, inventory rules are used to define the movement and management of stock within the warehouse. These rules determine how products are moved, how stock is allocated or reserved, and when to trigger certain actions like reordering or replenishing stock.

name: Issue with the 'Virtual Location' and 'Source Location' fields in the User Card when handling the multi-company scenario.

Issue with the 'Virtual Location' and 'Source Location' fields in the User Card when handling the multi-company scenario.

Table of Content

Issue with the 'Virtual Location' and 'Source Location' fields in the User Card when handling the multi-company scenario.IntroductionBackgroundIssue DescriptionImpactSolution ImplementationTechnical AdjustmentsConclusion Recommendations


Introduction

This document provides a detailed explanation of the customizations performed in the Odoo ERP system, specifically within the HelpDesk, Sales, and Purchase modules. It also addresses the issues encountered during the implementation of these customizations in a multi-company environment and outlines the solutions applied to resolve these issues.


Background

In the initial development, customizations were made in Odoo ERP for the HelpDesk module, introducing two new Many2One fields, 'Virtual Location' and 'Source Location' in the user card. The purpose of these fields was to assign default stock locations to users, which would be automatically recorded in the HelpDesk ticket form when a ticket was created by that user. These default locations were later used in logic and validations throughout the HelpDesk process.


Initially, this worked well in a single-company environment. However, in multi-company scenarios, the original design was no longer feasible because the user card was shared across companies, and it was impossible to assign different default locations to the same user based on the company.


Issue Description

When the system was extended to support multiple companies, a limitation was encountered. Since the user card is shared across all companies in Odoo, assigning different stock locations for the same user, company-wise, was not possible. This created conflicts in the HelpDesk process, as the correct locations could not be dynamically assigned based on the active company.

Impact

  • HelpDesk Module: The recorded locations in HelpDesk tickets were incorrect for users working across different companies, disrupting the HelpDesk workflows.
  • Data Integrity: The inability to differentiate location assignments for users across companies caused issues in validating ticket processes, leading to potential misrouting of HelpDesk tasks.


Solution Implementation

To resolve the issue, the original customization was modified to handle the multi-company scenario. Since the environment consisted of only two companies and there was no expectation for more, the following solution was implemented:


  • Creation of Additional Fields: Two new Many2One fields(stock.location) were created for 'Virtual Location' and 'Source Location' in the user card. These fields were identical in behavior to the original ones but were company-specific.


  •  New Field to Track Logged-In Company: A new field was added to the 'res.users' model to track the logged-in company in the user form.

​
  • Field Visibility Control: The visibility of these fields was controlled based on the logged-in company. This allowed users to view and manage only the fields relevant to their active company, ensuring that the correct locations were recorded for each company.


  • HelpDesk Ticket Adjustment: In the HelpDesk ticket form, the correct locations were dynamically pulled based on the logged-in company of the user, ensuring that the appropriate logic and validations were applied throughout the HelpDesk process.

  • Adjusting Custom Logic:

​The custom logic in the affected modules was reviewed and modified to accommodate the multi-company setup. This involved ensuring that  ​the logic could correctly identify and apply the appropriate default values based on the active company context.

Technical Adjustments

  • User Card: Two additional Many2One fields were added for both 'Virtual Location' and 'Source Location', with company-specific visibility rules applied.
  • HelpDesk Module: The HelpDesk ticket logic was modified to correctly fetch and apply the location fields based on the current company context.


Conclusion

The issue was resolved by adding company-specific fields for stock locations in the user card and controlling their visibility based on the logged-in company. This modification allowed users to manage distinct locations across multiple companies without compromising the original functionality. The HelpDesk process now correctly applies the appropriate location-based logic for each company. 


Recommendations

Future Developments: For any future customizations involving default values or user-specific fields in Odoo, especially in a multi-company environment, it is important to account for company-specific behaviors. Ensure thorough testing across all companies to avoid potential conflicts in logic or validation processes.

Bank Data ( Paymaster File )

User Manual: Master Data Setup & Excel Export Guide
Jinasena Agricultural Machinery (Pvt) Ltd  |  Odoo 17  |  Generated: 4/23/2026, 8:55:56 AM

Contents

  1. Bank Master Data — Add Bank with MICR Code
  2. Employee Bank Accounts — Add Account & Branch Code
  3. Link Bank Account to Employee
  4. Payslip Configuration Fields
  5. Bank Data Report — View & Verify
  6. Export to Excel & Paste to Paymaster
  7. Data Flow Reference — Where Each Column Comes From

1Bank Master Data — Add Bank with MICR Code

The MICR code is the bank identifier used in the CBC payment file (Column B — Dest Bank). It must be configured on every bank record that your employees use.

What is a MICR code? It is the 4-digit code assigned by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka to identify each bank. For example, Sampath Bank = 7054, Commercial Bank = 7010, HNB = 7728.
Step 1

Navigate to Banks

Go to: Accounting → Configuration → Banks

Step 2

Open a Bank Record or Create New

Click on an existing bank to edit, or click New to create.

  • Name — Full bank name (e.g. "Commercial Bank of Ceylon PLC")
  • BIC/SWIFT — International SWIFT code (optional)
  • MICR Code — Required for paymaster file. Enter the 4-digit CBC MICR code.
Important: If the MICR Code field is not visible, it may have been added via Odoo Studio. Go to Settings → Studio and check the res.bank model for the field x_micr_code.

2Employee Bank Accounts — Add Account & Branch Code

Each employee needs a bank account record with their account number, branch code, and the linked bank. These details populate Columns B, C, and D of the paymaster file.

Step 1

Navigate to Employee Bank Accounts

Go to: Payroll → Configuration → Employee Bank Accounts

Step 2

Create or Edit a Bank Account

Click New and fill in the following fields:

  • Account Number — Employee's full bank account number → goes to Column D (Dest Account)
  • Account Holder — Select the employee (partner)
  • Bank — Select from bank master. The bank's MICR code will be used for Column B (Dest Bank)
  • Branch Code — 3-digit branch code of the employee's bank branch → goes to Column C (Dest Branch)
Branch Code field: This is a custom Studio field x_branch_code on res.partner.bank. Make sure it is filled. It contains the 3-digit branch code (e.g. 089 for Sampath Colombo 3).

Field Mapping to Paymaster Columns

Paymaster ColumnSource Field
B — Dest Bank (MICR)Bank → MICR Code (x_micr_code)
C — Dest BranchBranch Code (x_branch_code)
D — Dest AccountAccount Number (acc_number)

3Link Bank Account to Employee

After creating the bank account, it must be linked to the employee record. Odoo uses this link to pull bank details into payslips automatically.

Step 1

Open the Employee Record

Go to: Payroll → Employees → Click on the employee

Step 2

Go to Private Information Tab

Click the Private Information tab on the employee form.

  • Find the Save & Close or Bank Account field
  • Select or create the employee's bank account here
  • This links the account so payslips can pull the destination bank details automatically
Tip: You can also add the bank account directly from this tab by clicking the Save icon next to the Bank Account field and entering the account details inline.

4Payslip Configuration Fields

Several paymaster columns come directly from fields on the payslip form itself. These are mostly company-level fixed values (originator bank, company name) and transaction parameters (TRN code, value date). They need to be set on each payslip batch.

Step 1

Open a Payslip

Go to: Payroll → Payslips → Click on a payslip

Screenshot not captured for: Payslip form — showing bank data configuration fields
Step 2

Fill in the Bank Data Fields

The following fields appear on the payslip form and must be filled before generating the Bank Data export:

Originator (Company) Fields — usually fixed

Transaction Parameter Fields — set per batch

x_return_dateI — Return DateDDMMYY format
x_currency_codeK — CurrencySLR
x_value_dateR — Value DateYYMMDD format
x_particularsP — Particulars107
x_security_fieldS — Security123123
x_fillerT — Filler@
Sample payslip data (live from Odoo): 5 confirmed/paid payslips checked.
Sample: Employee B M L Fernando — Net Wage: Rs 76,930.4 — Orig Bank: 7098

Sample Payslip Data

PayslipEmployeeNet WageOrig BankOrig BranchValue DateTRN CodeDest BankDest Account
SLIP/038 B M L Fernando 76,930.4 7098 089 250531 77 3422 222222222222
SLIP/039 J M C Dilini 41,558.23 7098 089 250531 77 5623 111222233333
SLIP/040 D G Rathnayake 46,053.59 7098 089 250531 77 ⚠ Empty ⚠ Empty

⚠ Red cells indicate missing employee bank account data — see Sections 2 & 3.

5Bank Data Report — View & Verify

The Bank Data report is the list view in Odoo that shows all payslip rows with the exact columns needed for the paymaster file. Always verify this view before exporting.

Step 1

Navigate to Bank Data

Go to: Payroll → Reporting → Bank Data

Step 2

Verify the Data Before Exporting

  • Check that Dest Bank (B), Dest Branch (C), and Dest Account (D) are filled for all employees. Empty cells mean the employee's bank account is not configured (see Sections 2 & 3).
  • Check that Value Date (R) matches the payment date for this batch.
  • Check that Amount (J) matches the expected net wages.
  • The Orig Bank/Branch/Account (L, M, N) should be Jinasena's salary account details.
Filter by batch: Use the search bar to filter by payslip batch name (e.g. "May 2025") to see only the current month's records. Otherwise all historical payslips will be shown.

6Export to Excel & Paste to Paymaster

Once the Bank Data view looks correct, export it to Excel and paste the data into the CBC paymaster template.

Step 1

Select All Records

On the Bank Data list view, tick the checkbox in the header row to select all visible records. A banner will appear — click "Select all X records" to include records across all pages.

Step 2

Open Actions → Export

Click the Actions button in the toolbar → Select Export.

Screenshot not captured for: Actions menu with Export option
Step 3

Configure Export Columns

In the Export dialog:

  • Select XLSX format
  • Add the columns in order: Dest Branch (C) → Dest Bank (B) → Dest Account (D) → Dest Name (E) → TRN Code (F) → Return Code (G) → Cr/Dr (H) → Return Date (I) → Amount (J) → Currency (K) → Orig Bank (L) → Orig Branch (M) → Orig Account (N) → Orig Name (O) → Particulars (P) → Reference (Q) → Value Date (R) → Security (S) → Filler (T)
  • Click Export to download the file
Screenshot not captured for: Export dialog — column selection
Step 4

Paste into Paymaster Excel Template

  • Open the CBC Paymaster Excel template
  • Open the Odoo exported XLSX
  • Copy all data rows (excluding the header) from the Odoo export
  • Paste into the paymaster template starting from Column B, Row 2
  • Verify the column order matches exactly
  • Save and submit to the bank
Column order check: The Odoo Bank Data columns (B through T) should map directly to the paymaster template columns in the same order. The column letters in the Odoo view headers match the paymaster file specification letters.

7Data Flow Reference — Where Each Column Comes From

Complete reference table showing exactly which Odoo field feeds each paymaster file column, where to enter the data, and the technical model path.

Col Paymaster Label Odoo Field Data Source Where to Enter / How it Gets There Technical Path Example Value

C Dest Branch x_dest_branch Employee Bank Account Payroll → Config → Employee Bank Accounts → open account → Branch Code field res.partner.bank.x_branch_code 878

M Orig Branch x_orig_branch Company bank — payslip field Jinasena's bank branch code. Set on the payslip form. Usually fixed at 089. hr.payslip.x_orig_branch 089
N Orig Account x_orig_account Company bank — payslip field Jinasena's own salary payment bank account number. Set on the payslip form. hr.payslip.x_orig_account 21321324442
O Orig Name x_orig_name Company name — payslip field Company name as it should appear in the bank file. Set on the payslip form. hr.payslip.x_orig_name JINASENA (PVT) LTD
P Particulars x_particulars Payslip field Set directly on the payslip form. Usually 1. hr.payslip.x_particulars 107
Q Reference x_cbc_reference Payslip reference Auto-populated from the payslip name/sequence. Can be edited on the payslip form. hr.payslip.x_cbc_reference Salary Slip - B
R Value Date x_value_date Payslip field The date the payment should be credited. Set on the payslip form. Format: YYMMDD. hr.payslip.x_value_date 250531
S Security x_security_field Payslip field Security code for the CBC file. Set on the payslip form. hr.payslip.x_security_field 123123

Legend: Employee Bank Account — Set up once per employee in Payroll → Configuration → Employee Bank Accounts
Employee — Pulled automatically from the employee record
Payslip field — Set on each payslip (transaction parameters for this batch)

Payroll calculation — Calculated automatically by Odoo payroll rules

Enterprise resource planning (ERP) is used by a company to manage key parts of its business such as accounting, manufacturing, sales, and marketing.

 

Information is the key to everything. Nobody can argue with that. The ability to get useful information at the right time can separate a successful company from a bankrupt one. That’s why every ERP implements the flexible, on demand report system.

​ ​ ​Route​

Odoo’s pre-configured routes are available in the warehouses’ menu. To find it, go to Inventory ‣ Configuration ‣ Warehouses. There, open your warehouse and edit it to see the pre-configured routes for incoming and outgoing shipments.

Some more advanced routes are already configured to make your work easier. Those are based on your choice for shipments. Once you made your choice, Inventory ‣ Configuration ‣ Routes to see the routes Odoo generated for you.

How to Setup Warehouse

 Warehouse and Warehouse operation.

​In Odoo, a Warehouse is the actual building/place in which your items are stocked. You can setup multiple warehouses and ​create moves between warehouses.

  • How to Create and process Batch & wave Transfers.

Batch transfer allows handling batch of orders which means you can regroup several transfers in to the same batch transfer and process them together.

 There are two types transfers.

1. Batch Transfers

​Can be use for managing delivery orders, receipt and internal transfers reduce the time taken for transportation 

2. Wave Transfers

( Only batch transfer is suitable for our company )

About Batch Transfer

The ETF Schedule is a reporting view that lists all Employees' Trust Fund (ETF) contributions posted to accounting. It is not a standalone payroll object — it is a filtered view of account.move.line (accounting journal entry lines) that were automatically created when payslips were confirmed.

name: Implement Multi-Company Feature in Custom Modules
body:
Implement Multi-Company Feature in Custom Modules

IntroductionBackgroundIssue DescriptionImpactSolution ImplementationTechnical AdjustmentsConclusion Recommendations


Introduction

This document provides a detailed explanation of the customizations performed in the Odoo ERP system, specifically within the HelpDesk, Sales, and Purchase modules. It also addresses the issues encountered during the implementation of these customizations in a multi-company environment and outlines the solutions applied to resolve these issues.


Background

In the initial development phase of our Odoo ERP, several custom modules were developed for both master data and transaction data. However, we did not initially account for the multi-company concept, which became necessary as we began managing data across different companies. To address this limitation, we implemented a series of customizations to our custom modules, as well as some base product models, to accommodate multi-company functionality.


Issue Description

The primary issue was the absence of multi-company considerations in both the master and transaction data models. Without these considerations, users were unable to properly segregate and manage data across multiple companies. Additionally, in some base product models, the multi-company concept was either partially implemented or entirely absent. For example:
  • Product Template (product.template): The company field existed, but automated features like defaulting the company based on the logged-in user were not implemented.
  • Product Categories (product.category): The multi-company concept was not applied at all.

 

Impact

  • Data Segregation: Without the ability to filter and assign records based on the company, users were unable to correctly manage data in a multi-company environment, leading to confusion and potential data integrity issues.
  • Visibility Issues: Records that should have been company-specific were visible to all companies, creating compliance and operational challenges.


Solution Implementation

To address these issues, the following customizations were applied across approximately 150 custom models: 


  • Company Field Addition: 


​A new Many2One field(accounting_company_id/ res.company) labeled as "Company" was introduced in both master and transaction tables. This ​field was added at the design level to ensure that each record is properly associated with a company. ​


  • Automated Company Assignment:

​An automated action was created to automatically fill the company_id field based on the current logged-in company. This ensures that all ​records are correctly associated with the user’s active company without requiring manual input.

​

	​company_id = env.context.get('allowed_company_ids', [env.user.company_id.id])[0]

​company = env['res.company'].browse(company_id)

​record['accounting_company_id'] = company.id


  • Record Rules for Company-Wise Visibility:

​A record rule was implemented for each model to control the visibility of records, ensuring that users only see records associated with their ​logged-in company.

 	​['|', ('accounting_company_id', 'in', company_ids), ('accounting_company_id', '=', False)]
  • Base Product Models:

​For base models like product.template (Product Master), multi-company features were extended. The company_id field already existed, but we ​implemented the automated action to fill the company field based on the logged-in company.


​For models like product.category (Product Categories), where the multi-company concept was entirely absent, we applied the same ​ ​ ​customizations done to our custom models: adding a company field, implementing automated company assignment, and creating record rules ​for company-wise visibility.


  • Additional Considerations:

​We implemented these changes across approximately 150 custom models, ensuring that multi-company functionality is applied uniformly.

​Please find attached the template for the full list.

Models (ir.model).xlsx
xlsx
Base Prodcut Masters (Company_Id Dev).xlsx
xlsx


Technical Adjustments

  • Company Field Addition: Added the company_id field in custom master and transaction tables to allow company-based segregation of data.
  • Automated Actions: Created automated actions to assign the company_id based on the logged-in company, ensuring the correct company is associated with each record.
  • Record Rules: Defined record rules for each model to enforce company-wise visibility, preventing cross-company data exposure.


Conclusion

By implementing the above three main customizations—adding the company field, automating company assignment, and defining record rules—we successfully adapted our Odoo ERP custom modules to handle multi-company scenarios. Additionally, we extended these customizations to certain base product models where the multi-company concept was either incomplete or missing altogether. These changes have stabilized data management processes across multiple companies, ensuring data integrity and compliance with company-specific operations. 


Recommendations

Future Developments: For any future Odoo ERP customizations, particularly in a multi-company setup, it is essential to account for company-specific behaviors from the outset. This includes adding the necessary fields, automating actions, and defining record rules to ensure accurate and secure data handling.

Introduction

Welcome to the user manual for the Special Projects module in Odoo ERP system!

This manual is your comprehensive guide to effectively managing and overseeing special projects within our organization. Special projects typically involve unique initiatives that require detailed planning, resource allocation, and meticulous execution over extended periods. For any type of project, this guide provides step-by-step instructions and functional guidance on utilizing the ERP system to streamline project workflows. From project setup and management to budget tracking, and comprehensive reporting, empower yourself with the tools and knowledge needed to optimize project management processes and achieve successful outcomes. Whether you're a project manager, team member, or administrator, this manual equips you with the essential skills to navigate and leverage the Special Projects module effectively.

 

Related Apps for Jinasena Projects

Sales App

To create the initial Sale Order with at least one Service Item that is configured to create a project on quotation confirmation, and with other inventory items and expense items that will all together makes the total project value.

Project App

To monitor the Project progress.

Invoice App

To create and post the project Invoices and receive payments for each invoice.

Accounting

To create Journal entries for expense handling.

Expenses App

To Create the Expense ( Service ) Product

 

Project Quotation

The life cycle of the project process starts by creating a Project Quotation. There may be multiple quotations which the main quotation is created initially with at least one Service Item that is configured to create a project on quotation confirmation, and with other inventory items, expense items, and items that are used to add provisions for expenses, that will all together makes the total project value. To create project quotations, the same quotation form that is in the Sales app is used and to identify project quotations separately the field “Quotation Type” is set as “Project”.

Creating a Project Quotation.

  • Select the Sales App.

The quotation form is opened with a list of quotations that have already been created. This list consists of both sales and project quotations that are created or already confirmed.

  • Click CREATE to create a new project quotation.


On the new Quotation, you will see the following fields that need to be filled in

Fields in the header section:

  • Customer: Select the name of the client.
    By the time this project quotation is created, the customer record for the client must have been created under Contacts. Depending on the information provided in the contact record, the Invoice Address, Delivery Address, Payment Terms, and Delivery Method will populated from the contact’s record, but can still be manually edited if needed.
  • Quotation Template: This is a quotation template that is to be created previously with a selected set of items. If the quotation template is selected in this form, the items that are already in the quotation template, will be automatically added to the current quotation. This may be useful for projects which similar set of items are being consumed or if common templates are created with common set of frequently used items for each project category.
  • Quotation Type: Select "Project" type from the drop-down list.​
    When “Project” is selected as the Quotation Type, the following additional fields will be included in the quotation form.
    • Project Group
    • Contract Start Date
    • Contract End Date
    • Project Budget

The completed “Other Info” tab:

 

Tab “Order Lines”:

This is the section where the quotation lines are entered. Here, below mentioned types of items are added.

·         The service item for the profit margin. This item is mandatory.

·         Existing Inventory items having on-hand stock.

·         Existing Inventory items that are out of stock.

·         New inventory items that are not available in the product master.

Ø  Enter each item with the above types in the fields mentioned below.

Ø  To start adding products, click on “Add a product”.

(Note: In addition to adding items, the added items can be separated in to sections by using the “Add a section”. By using “Add a note”, any special notes can be inserted in between lines.)

Product: The item that will be consumed to the project. Once the product is selected, the system fills in other related information based on the product master. Some of them can be manually edited in the quotation line.

Description: The item description from the Products master record is filled automatically and can be changed in the quotation line if required.

Trans Type: The product category from the Products master record is filled automatically and not editable.

Category: The Expense Category which the cost of the item or the expanse should be reflected in reports.

Quantity: The quantity to be entered by the user.

After saving, the quotation number is allocated. For project quotations, the suffix “_PRJ” is added at the end of the quotation number as in the next screenshot.

Getting the Last Purchased Cost of an item

If the last purchased price is to be set for inventory item in the quotation lines, the last purchased price can be retrieved from the item itself.

Ø  Click on the item in the quotation line to open the item or open the item directly.

Ø  Click on the smart button “More” > Purchased.


 

Having new Inventory Items or existing Inventory Items that are out of stock:

New Inventory Items:

When there are new items to be included in the quotation, that are not in our Items master, first, the user can enter the new item name in the quotation line. Then the system will ask whether to create the new item. On user’s confirmation, the item is created. Then the item is to be completed by the inventory users and an approval process is carried out. Once the new items are approved, they are treated as existing items that are out of stock and from this point onwards, the below mentioned process for “Inventory Items that are out of stock:” will be carried out.

Inventory Items that are out of stock:

If any item that was added is out of stock, it is required to get the current cost in to the “Cost Value” of the quotation line. For this, a Purchase Request (PR) is created from the quotation. Then from the PR, an RFQ is to be created. The RFQs to be sent to multiple vendors and based on their quotations the prices are to be updated in RFQs. Out of these RFQs, one RFQ should be finalized and the prices in the finalized RFQ are retrieved in to the quotation.

Adding a new inventory item

New Item Code: 05EC 060

Item Name : PVC FLEX. CABLE 6mm Sq.

Ø  In quotation lines, click “Add a product” and type the item name. Then click on “Create …”.

Ø  Then enter the Category and the quantity and SAVE.

The new item is created. But it is not yet completed by the inventory team and approved. Therefore the approval of the new item to be done prior to proceeding with the project quotation.

Item approval status:

Until the new items are approved, the approval status can be monitored by the Project staff.

Ø  Click PROJECT ITEM APPROVAL STATUS.

System will display a list of items that are awaiting approvals.

Completion of the newly created item

Completion of the new items is carried out by Inventory staff and it will be discussed in the Inventory module in detail.

Ø  Open the new item.

Navigation: Inventory > Menu > Products > Products > Filter the item > Open the item.

The Item form:

Ø  Fill the required information and click on REQUEST ITEM APPROVAL.

 

Approve new items

Once the approval request is made by a user, the APPROVE ITEM button appears. Then a user who has approval rights can approve the new item.

Ø  Click APPROVE ITEM to approve the new item.

After the new items that are created through the project are approved, in a project, they are treated as existing inventory items that are out of stock. Then the operations with the project can be proceeded further.

 

Adding existing inventory items that are out of stock:

Adding inventory items that are already in the Items Master that are out of stock is as same as adding items that are having stocks. But if such items are added in a quotation, it is required to retrieve the latest item prices (Costs). To achieve this, Purchase requests can be created through the project quotation and then, from the PRs, the RFQs can be created. Then RFQs to be sent to multiple vendors and receive quotations. Then quoted prices are to be input in each RFQ and the selected RFQ is to be updated as finalized. Thereafter the quoted prices can be retrieved in to the project quotation lines. The cost prices will be updated in the quotation line, in the field “Cost Value”.

 

Sub-Contracting

Sub-contracts are the services that are out-sourced to a third party vendor. To achieve this, separate subcontract service items with item names that are relevant to subcontracts are used in the project quotation. These items can be distinguished from others by the field “Sub-Contract” in the “General” tab of the items master.

For subcontracts, on confirmation of the quotation, a single Purchase Request is created from the project quotation including all the subcontract items, and from these purchase requests, multiple RFQs can be created for multiple vendors who provides each service and the selected RFQs are finalized and converted as Purchase Orders. The purchase orders are invoiced as per the vendor invoices, and the payments can be processed directly through the posted PO invoices.

Adding Subcontracting items to the project

Add sub-contract items:

Subcontract items are added in to project quotations in the same way which the other inventory items are added by clicking on “Add a product”.

 


 

Creating Purchase Requests

Purchase Requests are created for new items, items without stocks and subcontracts.

Open the project quotation.

Before creating the purchase request, in quotation lines, for new items and existing items without stock, the Purchase Type should be filled in the quotation lines. This is to mention whether the items are to be imported or purchased locally, which is a required information when creating RFQs from PRs.

Ø  Fill the Purch. Type.

 

Click CREATE PR to create the purchase request.

Click OK.

Note: By now, if the Purchase Types of quotation lines are not filled for required items, the below error will be displayed.

​

Click on each record to open each Purchase Request.

Purchase request for out-of-stock items. ​

Purchase request for all the subcontracts.

 

Proceed with the Purchase Request for items that are out of stock.

Create RFQ from Purchase Request.

RFQs are created from the Purchase Request. The Purchase Request can be opened through the project quotation or directly from the home screen.

Navigation 1: Project quotation > Smart button “PRs” > Select the Purchase request

Navigation 2: Home screen > Purchase Requisitions app > filter by the PR number.

Once the PR is opened, the button CREATE RFQ button is available.

Ø  Click CREATE RFQ button.

The intermediate screen will pop up allowing the user to select the vendor and the items that we expect to receive prices from the selected vendor.

Ø  Select the vendor and then select which items are to be included in the RFQ.

Ø  Then click CREATE RFQ.

 

The system will display the newly created RFQ.


Ø  Click on the created RFQ record, to open it.

 


 

The newly created RFQ:

Ø  Using these buttons SEND BY EMAIL or PRINT RFQ, send the RFQ by email directly to the vendor, or download as a PDF and then send as an email attachment using the email

Ø  Then send the RFQs to the vendors and when the quotations are received, update the prices and tax percentages in each RFQ, as in the quotations.

Uploading the softcopies of the Quotations to the system.

Once the quotations are received, before going forward, the prices should be updated in the RFQs as mentioned above, and the softcopies of the quotation must be uploaded to the system.

Ø  In the RFQ, select the “Documents” tab.

Ø  Click EDIT.

Ø  In the “Documents” tab, click UPLOAD YOUR FILE.

Ø  Brows and select the quotation file and click “Open” to upload it.

​

Update the RFQ as Quotation Received.

Ø  Click RECEIVE QUOTATION.

Then the “Receive Status” will become “Received”.

 

 

Note: If the RECEIVE QUOTATION button is clicked without before uploading the quotation file, the below error will be displayed saying “Quotation copy must be uploaded”.

 

The Receive Status will be updated as “Received” and the button UPDATE PR appears.

Similarly, from one Purchase Requisition, multiple RFQs can be created for the same set of items, and quotations can be called from multiple vendors and updated in each RFQ. Then they can be evaluated and once an RFQ finalized, it must be updated in the system.

Finalizing an RFQ

From multiple RFQs, once an RFQ finalized, it must be updated in the system by clicking UPDATE PR button. By doing so, any other RFQ that was created for the same PR items, cannot be proceeded there onwards.

Ø  Click UPDATE PR.

Note: In the Projects module, the RFQs that are created for non-stock items, are only for costing purposes. Therefore, such RFQs cannot be confirmed, and move forward as Purchase Orders to proceed with the purchases. The items that are to be purchased for projects, to be handled by the Inventory side and the purchased goods will be received in to the inventory and transferred to the project warehouse to consume for projects.

The costs received from quotations, are to be retrieved to the project quotation, only after completing the RFQs that covers all the PR lines. Therefore, the process of RFQs for non-stock items ends here.

 

Proceed with the Purchase request for all the subcontracts.

Open the purchase request for subcontracts

Navigation: Project Quotation > Smart button: PRs

The 2 PRs that were created from the quotation are displayed as bellow.


Ø  Click and open the Purchase Request for the subcontract.

The Purchase Request for Subcontracts:

Confirm the Purchase Request

​

A user who has PR approval rights can approve this PR Approve the Purchase Request

Ø  Click APPROVE

 

Creating Subcontract RFQs

​

Ø  Click CRAETE RFQ

The newly created RFQ:

 

Specifications of the requirement

If any specific details of the requirement are to be mentioned that are in images, or any other document, such details can be attached to the RFQ.

Sending the RFQ to the supplier.

Once the RFQ form is complete, it can be sent to the suppliers.

Ø  Using these buttons SEND BY EMAIL or PRINT RFQ, send the RFQ by email directly to the vendor, or download as a PDF and then attach it to an email and send using the email application in the computer.

Ø  When the quotations are received from suppliers, update the prices and tax percentages in each RFQ, as in the quotations.

Uploading softcopies of the Quotations to the system.

Once the quotations are received, before going forward, the prices should be updated in the RFQs as mentioned above, and the softcopies of the quotation must be uploaded to the system.

Ø  In the RFQ, select the “Documents” tab.

Ø  Click EDIT.

Ø  In the “Documents” tab, click UPLOAD YOUR FILE.
