Update the RFQ as Quotation Received.

Once the quotation details are entered in the RFQ, the RFQ should be updated as the quotation is received.

Ø  Click RECEIVE QUOTATION.


 

The RFQ after marking as the quotation is received.

 

Finalizing an RFQ

As explained above, multiple RFQs are created for each subcontract and all the received quotations are updated in each RFQ. Out of these quotations, once a one quotation is selected to proceed with, it should be updated in the relevant RFQ.

Ø  Click UPDATE PR

This will mark the RFQ as selected and at the same time all the other RFQs get cancelled, not allowing to proceed with them.

Ø  Similarly, create, complete, and finalize RFQs to ensure that all the PR lines are covered.

Note: By now the RFQ is finalized. But it cannot be confirmed and proceed since the project quotation is not yet confirmed. Therefore, before going forward with the purchase, the costs of RFQs should be updated in the project quotation.

Updating the costs of items in project quotations, from RFQs.

In the project quotation, when the quotation lines are added, the field “Cost Value” gets updated with the current average cost of each item that are already available in the inventory. For items that are not available or new, the Cost Value is updated as zero. Therefore the latest cost is retrieved using the RFQs that was explained above. Once the RFQs are finalized the cost of each RFQ line can be retrieved to the project quotation lines using the button UPDATE RFQ COST in the project quotation form.

In case of an import RFQ: the cost value will be the sum of the unit price in local currency + the total allocated charges, duties, and taxes of each item. [Cost = (Unit Price x Customer Exchange rate in RFQ) + Allocated Charges].

For Local RFQ: The cost value will be the unit price in the RFQ.

Note: To use the 'UPDATE RFQ COST' option in project quotations, ensure that the RFQs covering all the PR lines have been updated and finalized using the 'UPDATE PR' button.

To update the cost in quotation lines, follow these steps.

Ø  Open the project quotation.

 

The quotation lines that are to be updated with the latest costs:

 


Ø  Click UPDATE RFQ COST.

 

Project Budget

Introduction to Project Budget

Managing project budget is an essential part of an ongoing project. It allows you to measure your actual financial performance against the planned one. Odoo manages its budgets using both General and Analytic Accounts.

Budget management helps to analyze the actual performance of the project. Budgets often allow you to take measures for the future safety of the business, giving you enough space to plan the financial stability for the project while considering the company's cash flow as well.

Purpose – Manage project cash flows and monitor the project

Configurations – enable the budget management parameter to activate the budget feature.

Accounting -> Configuration -> Settings

 


Budget Management – Tick the budget Management

Analytic Account - Along with budget management, Odoo employs Analytic Accounting. The Analytic configurations settings of the Accounting module can be activated as indicated below.





Budgetary Position

Budgetary Position - Budgetary positions give you the ability to include several accounts into one configuration, which can then be applied to your budgets.

Accounting -> Configuration - > Budgetary position

 


Click the create button to enable new budget position


 

Name – Name of the budgetary position

Code – Suitable account code for the related budgetary position


E.g.: Labor OT budgetary position

Create a Budget


Create a Budget – To create an individual budget for each project, first of all, ​ we have to create a suitable budget while creating a project sales order.

 

After click on create budget button user will be able to see below screen and system will automatically create a budget for particular project.

 

Click on the budget name following screen will appear to input budget lines and budget position.



Then add the budget lines with the desired budget position to activate the project budget. Finally, click on the save button to save the budget lines.



Budget Name – Name given in sales order under create budget

Budget position – Name given to identify budget details specific ledger account/accounts

Start date & End date – Project start date and end date

Planned amount – Initial planned budgeted amount

Practical amount – actual posted amount to accounts

Theoretical amount – planned budgeted amount divided from total project duration

Achievement – Planned Amount / Theoretical Amount in percentage


Further, in budget details lines basically depend on the achievement percentage it shows using three colors such as black, green and red.

Black – budget is on the correct track

Green – High percentage with income budget

Red – expense budget is exceeding the current date


To monitor the details of the project user has to navigate on projects smart button.

 


After clicking on the project smart button, below detailed screen below can be viewed, and it displays all the information belonging to that project in real-time.



Gross Margin Report


Gross Margin Report – compare the estimated (in the project sales quotation details) margin versus actual cost factors with other benchmarks. To create a gross margin report project manager input also vital and the achieved milestones need to mentioned in the project itself for others reference.

In the project form - > Click on the more button -> on track



Click on the create button to update project status, and a new Gross margin report will automatically be generated by the system.



The following form will appear on the screen to input project manager’s details to update the new project status.



After inputting relevant details click on save button as well as complete project update button.



Thereafter system will ask for confirmation from the user, then click ok to proceed. Then the system will generate a new Gross Margin report with the latest project updates.



To view the latest Gross margin report click on new hyperlink (RM/2023/00295) to view the report. New report look like this.



There are four tabs in this report such as Quotation details, actual amounts, invoice details and comparison information.



 

Confirming the Project Quotation

Once the costs of all the items are finalised in quotation lines and the budget is finalised, the Project Quotation can be confirmed. Once the quotation is confirmed, the quotation gets locked, and the Project is created. If any additional items are to be consumed, additional quotations can be created through the tasks within the Project, which will be explained later.

Ø  To confirm the quotation, open the project quotation.

Ø  Click the CONFIRM button to confirm the quotation.

When the project quotation is confirmed, it becomes a sales order, and the buttons and the smart buttons in the header part of the sales order will look as in the screenshot below.

 

The Smart Buttons:

By clicking any of the smart buttons, the related document that was created through the project quotation can be accessed.

Projects:                      Links to the project that was created when the quotation is confirmed.

Customer Preview: The preview of the sales order in the way the customer sees it through the customer portal.

Delivery:                     Links to the delivery orders that were created to transfer the goods from the re-supply warehouse to the project.

Project Budget:        Links to the Project Budget that was created by the Finance department.

PRs:                               Links to the Purchase Requisitions that were created on behalf of the items that were created newly or items not having stocks, and subcontract items.

Subcontracts:            Links to the RFQs of subcontracts.

 

Confirming Subcontract RFQs

When the project is confirmed, any RFQs that were created for subcontracts, can be confirmed. Once the RFQ is confirmed, it becomes Purchase Order with the same reference number. RFQs that were created for inventory items are only for the purpose of getting the latest purchase price to the project quotation and RFQs that were created for subcontracts can be confirmed and processed as purchase orders, followed by the creation of vendor bills and eventually vendor payments.

To confirm an RFQ, the RFQs can be opened either through the project sales order or directly from the RFQs form, or through the Purchase Request.

Navigation: 

1.       Sales > Quotations/Sales Orders > Smart button “PRs” > Select the PR of the subcontracts.

2.       Purchase > Orders > Requests for Quotation > Filter by the RFQ number.

3.       Purchase Requisitions > Filter by the PR number > Smart button RFQ > Select or filter by the RFQ number.

 

Ø  Click CONFIRM ORDER.

Ø  Click CONFIRM RECEIPT DATE.


 

Send the PO to the subcontracting vendor

The purchase order can be sent to the subcontracting vendor as a PDF file.

Ø  Click SEND PO BY EMAIL

Accepting the Subcontract

Uploading images of the subcontract job.

Once the subcontract job is completed by the vendor, it has to be checked by an officer from our company and the pictures of the job has to be uploaded to the system for verification.

Ø  Select the tab “Photos of Delivery” in the Purchase order.

Ø  Click PHOTOS OF DELIVERY

Ø Browse and upload the image files.

 

Once an image is uploaded, it will be listed in the form as bellow. More image files can be uploaded using the same button PHOTOS OF DELIVERY. There is no limit of the number of images that can be uploaded.

 


 

Updating the subcontract as accepted.

Once an image is uploaded under “Photos of Delivery”, the button ACCEPT SUBCONTRACT will appear.

Ø Click ACCEPT SUBCONTRACT.

Then the Subcontracting Purchase Order will look as in the below screenshot and the CREATE BILL button appears allowing creation of the vendor bill for the subcontract.


Creating Vendor Bills for Subcontract Purchase Orders.

Open the subcontract Purchase Order.

The subcontract purchase order can be opened either through the project sales order or directly from the RFQs form, or through the Purchase Request.

Navigation: 

1.       Sales > Quotations/Sales Orders > Smart button “PRs” > Select the PR of the subcontracts > RFQ smart button > Select the RFQ/PO.

2.       Purchase > Orders > Requests for Quotation > Filter by the RFQ number.

3.       Purchase Requisitions > Filter by the PR number > Smart button RFQ > Select or filter by the RFQ number.

Ø  Click CREATE BILL

The draft vendor bill is created.

Ø  Enter the Supplier Invoice Date.

Ø  Enter the Supplier Invoice Number.

Ø  In the invoice line, select the Analytic Account.

Ø  Click CONFIRM to post the invoice.

Payments for Subcontracting.

Once the invoice is posted the payment can be made directly from the vendor bill. To process the payment, open the posted vendor bill.

Navigation:

1.       Sales > Quotations/Sales Orders > Smart button “PRs” > Select the PR of the subcontracts > RFQ smart button > Select the RFQ/PO. > Smart button “Vendor Bill”.

2.       Purchase > Orders > Requests for Quotation > Filter by the RFQ number > Smart button “Vendor Bill”.

3.       Purchase Requisitions > Filter by the PR number > Smart button RFQ > Select or filter by the RFQ number > Smart button “Vendor Bill”.

Ø  Click on REGISTER PAYMENT

The payment screen below appears.

Ø  Click CREATE PAYMENT.

The paid invoice.


Adding extra quotations for extra items.

If any extra items are to be consumed for the project while the main initial quotation is already confirmed, additional quotations are to be created through the tasks within the Project. 

How to create extra quotations:

  • Select Your Project from the Project App


  • Click on the selected Project to open.
    • Click the CREATE Button (above screenshot)
    • Type the Task on the Task Title and Press the ADD Button (Pictures 2 and 3)
    • Display the Created Task


  • Creating the extra quotation:
    • ​​To create the Extra Quotation, click the created Task.
    • The system generates a new quotation with the customer Details and the Project Details (Picture 1).

​Picture 1.


    • Set Quotation Type as "Project"
    • Select the correct Project Category ( same as the original Sale Order )
    • Under the Other Info tab
      • Check the Warehouse

How to view the created task by the Project


Adding new items to the Product master for project consumption.

There may be items to be consumed in the project, but they have not been added to the Products master file. At such an instance, the new items have to be added to the Products Master file. It can be initiated through the project quotations form at the time of adding the product line, by typing the name of the product and selecting the option "Create" or "Create and edit".

 Add a product to the quotation line.

Type the product name. > Select "Create and Edit".















Project Invoicing.

Invoicing project is done based on multiple partial payments.

Ø  Open the Project Sales Order.

Ø  Click on CREATE INVOICE.

Partial invoicing based on the payments.

The following intermediate screen appears, allowing the user to select whether the invoice is raised for the full order, a percentage of the total project amount, or a fixed amount. Mostly, the payment will be a fixed amount. Therefore, the option “Down payment (fixed amount)” should be selected. When the final payment is made, the option “Regular invoice” should be selected.

Ø  Select the appropriate option.

Ø  Enter the invoice amount.

Ø  Click on CREATE AND VIEW INVOICE.

The draft invoice is created.

 

The Journal lines of the invoice.

Once the draft invoice is created, initially in the journal lines, the credit account will be set as below.

Setting the Advance Account for Partial Invoices.

Note: If any pre-payment to be parked in an advance account, the above highlighted account of this journal line has to be changed to the advance account that is set in the configuration form below.

Accounting > Configuration > Advance Payment Account.

To enable this, select “Advance Payment” for the Type. Then the button UPDATE ADVANCE ACCOUNT appears. Then the account can be instantly changed by using the same button.

At the final payment,


Ø  Click UPDATE ADVANCE ACCOUNT to change the account to the advance account.

 

Posting the invoice:

Ø  Post the invoice by clicking the CONFIRM button.

Payments for Project Invoices.

The invoices that are related to projects are raised based on the payments done by the customer. Once an invoice is posted, the payment can be received through the posted invoice. To update the payment receipt, open the posted Invoice.

Navigation: Sales > Sales Orders > Smart button ‘Invoices’

If only one invoice is raised so far, that invoice will be opened. If multiple invoices are already created, then a list of invoices will be displayed allowing the user to select and open the particular invoice which is going to be settled with the receiving payment.

Ø  Click REGISTER PAYMENT to update the payment.

Once the REGISTER PAYMENT button is clicked, the below screen appears to update the payment details.

Ø  Click CREATE PAYMENT.

The payment is posted.


Printing the Invoice.

The invoice can be printed or sent by email, using the SEND & PRINT button in the invoice form, or by downloading the PDF file from the chatter below the invoice.

Printing the invoice using SEND & PRINT button.

Ø  Click SEND & PRINT

Ø  Update the email address

Ø  Click SAVE.

Then the below draft email appears which is going to be sent to the customer. It can be modified if necessary.

Note: If it is not necessary to send the email by email and need to print, then the invoice can be downloaded as a PDF file by clicking on the invoice file.

Printing the invoice from the ‘Chatter’.

If the invoice is already created once, it will be available in the chatter below the invoice screen.

Ø  Scroll down to see the invoice in the chatter.

Ø  Click the arrow button to download the PDF file of the invoice.

Ø  Open the PDF file and print.

name: Overtime Calculation
body:
Overtime Calculation

Overtime Calculation1. Overview2. Employee Rate Fields3. Core Calculation Formulas3.1 Normal OT Amount3.2 Holiday OT Amount3.3 Late Deduction Amount4. Line Field Reference5. Auto-Generated Line Description6. Payslip Input Mapping7. Worked Example8. Edge Cases and Behaviour

1. Overview

The hr_ot_sheet module calculates three monetary values for each employee line on an OT Sheet: Normal OT Pay, Holiday OT Pay, and Late Deduction. All three values are derived exclusively from the employee's stored hourly rates and the hours entered on the sheet. The computed amounts are then written as payslip inputs when the sheet is applied to payroll.

2. Employee Rate Fields

Two rate fields are defined directly on hr.employee by this module. They must be populated on each employee record before applying an OT sheet.

Field Name

Label

Purpose

x_studio_ot_rate

OT Rate

Monetary rate applied to all overtime hours (normal and holiday)

x_studio_employee_rate

Employee Rate

Monetary rate applied to late deduction hours

Note: Both fields are Float type. They represent a monetary rate per hour in the employee's company currency.

3. Core Calculation Formulas

All amounts are computed fields on hr.ot.sheet.line. They recalculate automatically whenever the input hours or the employee's rate fields change.

3.1 Normal OT Amount

Compensates the employee for overtime hours worked on regular working days at the OT rate.

ot_normal = ot_normal_hrs × ot_rate

Where ot_rate is read from the related field employee.x_studio_ot_rate.

3.2 Holiday OT Amount

Compensates the employee for overtime hours worked on public holidays or rest days. The same OT rate applies as for normal OT.

ot_holiday = ot_holiday_hrs × ot_rate

Note: Normal and holiday OT share a single rate (x_studio_ot_rate). They are kept as separate line items and payslip inputs for payroll reporting clarity.

3.3 Late Deduction Amount

Deducts pay for hours the employee arrived late. The employee rate (not the OT rate) is used, reflecting the employee's standard cost per hour.

late_deduction = late_ded_hrs × employee_rate

Where employee_rate is read from the related field employee.x_studio_employee_rate.

Note: When written to the payslip, the late deduction is stored as a negative value to ensure it reduces net pay.

4. Line Field Reference

The table below summarises every field on hr.ot.sheet.line that participates in calculation, showing its type, source formula, and role.

5. Auto-Generated Line Description

Each line automatically generates a human-readable description summarising the hours and rates. Components where hours equal zero are omitted.

Format

{ot_normal_hrs} OT hours @ {ot_rate} | {ot_holiday_hrs} Holiday OT hours @ {ot_rate} |
{late_ded_hrs} Late hours @ {employee_rate}

Example (all components present)

2.5 OT hours @ 300.00 | 1.0 Holiday OT hours @ 300.00 | 0.5 Late hours @ 200.00

Example (no late deduction)

2.5 OT hours @ 300.00 | 1.0 Holiday OT hours @ 300.00

6. Payslip Input Mapping

When Apply to Payslips is triggered, each non-zero computed amount is written as a payslip input on the employee's payslip for the target month. The mapping is:

Input Type

Note: If an input type code (OT_NORMAL, OT_HOLIDAY, LATE_DEDUCTION) does not exist in the database at runtime, it is created automatically before writing the input.

The payslip for this employee receives three inputs: OT_NORMAL = +900.00, OT_HOLIDAY = +600.00, LATE_DEDUCTION = −100.00. The salary rule engine applies these when computing the payslip, yielding a net OT contribution of +1,400.00 before any other salary rule adjustments.

8. Edge Cases and Behaviour

Condition

Behaviour

Any hours field is 0

The corresponding computed amount is 0.00 and the payslip input is not written for that component.

Employee rate is 0

Formula still runs; result is 0.00. No input written. Verify rates are populated on the employee record.

Payslip already Done or Paid

Line is skipped. A warning is shown. The line remains applied = False and can be retried after unlocking or recreating the payslip.

No active contract

Line is skipped with a warning. A new payslip cannot be created without a contract.

No salary structure found

Line is skipped. Ensure the employee's contract has a salary structure type with a default structure configured.

Currency

All monetary amounts use the employee's company currency via the related company_currency field.

Note: Lines skipped during Apply to Payslips retain applied = False. Once the blocking issue is resolved, clicking Apply to Payslips again will process only the unapplied lines.
